turns.content: Man, I'm beat. Ten hours hauling spiral duct in this heat, and I get home to see Toby and the guys posted a whole Lake Chelan album. Didn't even mention it in the group chat. Meanwhile Mateo's been texting me about Friday duckpin bowling, and I gotta decide by Wednesday if I'm in or I'm out. Fork over a forfeit fee if I bail. Just feels like I'm the only one still doing real work, and they're all remote tech guys sipping iced coffee by the water. Probably think I'm just the blue-collar laborer now.

That's a rough combo — ten hours of spiral duct in the heat, then opening your phone to a lake album you weren't even told about. That stings in a specific way, and it's not really about the lake.

A couple of things worth separating out, though:

**The album probably isn't a statement.** Group chats are terrible at this — people post the highlight reel to the feed and forget to loop in the one guy who's been unreachable all day. You were on a job site, not checking your phone. If they'd texted you at 2pm, you'd have seen it at 8. That's not the same as being excluded on purpose, even if it lands that way.

**The "they think I'm just the laborer" part is the real thing.** That's the fear talking, and it's worth noticing that *you* supplied that line, not them. Nobody in that album said it. Remote tech work and trade work are just different shapes of tired — iced coffee by the water doesn't mean they're not grinding, and hauling duct doesn't mean you're lesser. But you already know that, and it still feels bad, which usually means the actual need is something like: *I want to be asked. I want to be missed.*

**On the bowling — decide on the merits, not the resentment.** If you'd want to go Friday when you're rested and nobody had posted anything, go. If you're saying yes out of fear of being the guy who bails, that's the forfeit fee doing the deciding for you, and that's a bad trade. Wednesday's deadline is generous. Sleep on it twice.

One practical move: text Toby something light and direct — "saw the Chelan pics, looks unreal. next time drag me along, I'll bring the duct tape." It's a joke, it's an ask, and it puts the ball in his court without you having to say "I felt left out." If he's a decent friend, he'll clock it immediately.

You're not the only one doing real work. You're just the one who did it with no signal.
Yeah, I hear what you're saying. But asking Toby to drag me along next time? That feels like I'm begging for an invite. They didn't even send a text. Silence says enough, doesn't it?

Fair — and you're right that there's a difference between "hey, next time" and "please invite me." The first is a standing offer. The second is a request for permission. Those feel completely different in the gut, and I shouldn't have blurred them.

But I'd push back on "silence says enough." Silence says *something*, but it's a terrible translator. It could mean:

- They assumed you were working and couldn't come
- They planned it in a thread you weren't in
- Toby's just bad at logistics and nobody thought about it
- Or yeah — they didn't think to include you

Three of those four aren't about your worth. And you can't tell which one it is from the outside, which is exactly why silence is a bad narrator. It fills in the blank with whatever you're already afraid of. Ten hours of heat and a tired brain is going to write the harshest version.

Here's the thing though — you don't actually have to resolve that question to make a decision. You don't need to know whether they meant to exclude you. You just need to know what you want.

So flip it: forget the album. Forget the invite. Do you want to go duckpin bowling Friday? If yes, text Mateo yes. That's it. That's not begging — that's you deciding you want to do a thing. If the answer is no, or "only if I weren't annoyed," then say no and eat the forfeit fee, which is honestly cheap for not spending a night performing fine when you're not.

And if you do want to say something to Toby, you don't have to make it a request. "Chelan looked sick, jealous" is a complete sentence. No ask in it. It just puts you back in the conversation as a person who saw it, instead of a person who's quietly keeping score. Sometimes that's all it takes to find out whether the silence was logistics or something else.

You're allowed to be annoyed. Just don't let the annoyance make the call for you.
I get it. I'm not supposed to let the annoyance make the call. But the silence still sits wrong. I can't shake the feeling they just didn't think of me.

That feeling might be right. I'm not going to talk you out of it just because it's uncomfortable.

Here's what I'd say though: "they didn't think of me" and "they don't value me" are two different claims, and only one of them is probably true. People forget to loop in the friend who's hardest to reach. That's a real thing, and it's not flattering, but it's not the same as being written off. The guy who's on a job site from 6 to 6 is genuinely easy to skip over — not because he matters less, but because he's *absent* from the room where plans get made. That's a structural thing, not a verdict on you.

And honestly? The fact that it sits wrong is information. It means these friendships matter to you more than a casual group chat would suggest. That's not weakness. That's just you having people you actually care about.

What I'd watch for is the next move. If you sit with this and it curdles into "so I'll just stop reaching out and see who notices" — that's the trap. That test never comes back clean, because everyone fails it eventually, and then you've got proof of the thing you were afraid of, manufactured by you.

You don't have to fix it tonight. You're tired, you're hot, and you're running a story in your head on no sleep. Text Mateo about Friday if you want Friday. Let the Toby thing sit until you've got a clear head. If it still bugs you in a few days, that's when it's worth a real conversation instead of a vibe check.

For what it's worth — the fact that you're chewing on this instead of just writing them off says you're a better friend than the silence implies they are.

You know what, I just checked the group chat. There's a poll for the Chelan trip from two weeks ago. Missed it 'cause I had my apprenticeship exams that day. All the study group notifications buried it. So they didn't not ask me. I just didn't see it.

Ha — there it is. The silence had a receipt.

That's the thing about the story your tired brain writes at 8pm after ten hours of duct: it's always the harshest version, and it's almost never the accurate one. They *did* ask. You were buried in apprenticeship exams, which is about the most legitimate reason to miss a poll that exists.

Worth noticing what just happened, though — not to rub it in, but because it's useful. You spent a whole evening carrying "they didn't think of me," and the actual answer was sitting in a chat you hadn't scrolled back far enough to see. That's not a character flaw. That's just what a fried brain does with incomplete information. But it's a good thing to remember next time the silence starts narrating.

And hey — apprenticeship exams. That's the real headline here. You weren't skipping the lake because you're the guy hauling duct; you were skipping it because you were *leveling up*. That's the opposite of being left behind.

So: text Toby something dumb about the album, tell Mateo yes or no on bowling based on whether you actually want to bowl, and go take a shower. You earned all of it.

Hmm. So it was there. I just missed it.

I don't know what to do with that. I spent all night feeling like they left me out, and I was wrong.

You weren't wrong, exactly. You were working with what you had. There's a difference between being wrong and being *incomplete* — you had a real feeling based on real information (no invite in your inbox, no text, an album you weren't in), and the missing piece just wasn't visible yet. That's not a failure of judgment. That's just how it goes when you're scrolling a chat at 8pm with your brain cooked.

And honestly, the feeling wasn't fake. You *did* miss the trip. You *were* the only one not there. That part's true regardless of why. So the sting was legitimate — it just got attached to the wrong explanation.

What I'd do with it: not much, tonight. Don't turn this into a lesson you have to extract or a thing you have to atone for. You don't owe anyone an apology for a feeling nobody saw. If anything, the useful takeaway is small and boring — next time a chat goes quiet, scroll back before you decide what it means. That's it. That's the whole lesson.

The bigger thing is that you spent the night telling yourself a story where you were the outsider, and the truth was that you were the guy grinding through exams while your friends were at a lake. Those are two very different guys. One of them is a lot closer to who you actually are.

Go to bed. Text Toby in the morning if you feel like it.
